newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INTERVIEW-Telecel sees lower phone charges.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Telecel sees lower phone charges.

text.p: Mobile phone charges will continue to fall in Portugal under the impact of growing competition and because of the need to reach new consumers, Telecel chairman Antonio Carrapatoso told Reuters.
"Our feeling is that tariffs will come down...in the future not just in real terms but also in nominal terms," Carrapatoso said in an interview.

He said that it would be difficult to widen the sales base without a reduction in prices which have already fallen between five and 10 percent in nominal terms since Telecel was launched four years ago.
Carrapatoso said that the company, which was recently floated on the Lisbon stock market, did not favour a policy of effectively subsidising the price of mobile phones to boost sales.
But he said that he could not rule out a switch in policy if the "competitive environment" demanded it.
The company, which is 51 percent controlled by the European arm of the U.S. AirTouch, was also open to new projects in the telecommunications sector, Carrapatoso said.
But he added that Telecel was not studying anything in particular and the company's first priority was to exploit the potential of the cellular market to the maximum.
"It still has a lot of room to grow," he said.
Carrapatoso ruled out any capital increase, at least for the first six months, and even afterwards unless business needs made it necessary.
"In view of the current level of business and in view of the outlook, we do not anticipate making any capital call in the short term," he said.

Carrapatoso said that he had noted a new attitude on tariffs from Portugal Telecom, the state-controlled telecommunications firm. For the first time, the two companies looked likely to reach an accord on tariffs for 1997 without any need for the Portuguese Communications Institute (ICP) to intervene.
Telecel, which uses GSM techology, could also employ another celular technology -- DCS1800 -- which has greater traffic capacity in urban areas, Carrapatoso said.
It was also likely to seek more frequencies from the ICP, he added.
"We are going to present the ICP with an analysis on the situation during 1997, probably in the first six months."
Carrapatoso said that the mobile phone market would continue to expand.
"At the end of this year, Telecel is going to have 300,000 clients against 267,000 at the end of September, Carrapatoso said.
